title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
authors: Sridevi Kuriyattil, Johannes Kombe, Andrew J. Daley, Pablo M. Poggi
abstract: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.
summary: This work explores how tuning the initial symmetry of a long-range spin model can switch its dynamics between predictable collective behavior and rapid quantum scrambling. By analyzing entanglement and chaos indicators, the authors show that the initial state dictates the dynamics, offering a unified framework for controlling quantum information spreading in experimentally accessible systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the transition between two distinct quantum dynamical regimes—collective dynamics and fast scrambling—within a single, deterministic, long-range spin model.
main_result: The crossover between these two regimes is controlled not by the Hamiltonian itself, but by the initial state's degree of symmetry breaking, which can be tuned by local perturbations.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using entanglement measures (bipartite/multipartite entropy) and semiclassical diagnostics, specifically Lyapunov exponents extracted from Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs).
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional XY spin model with long-range couplings, studied on specific graphs like the Powers-of-two (PWR2) graph or power-law decaying graphs. The dynamics are controlled by perturbing a fully symmetric initial state.
key_observables: Bipartite and multipartite entanglement entropy ($S_A$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda_L$).
important_parameters: The fraction of flipped spins ($k/N$) controls the crossover, and the graph structure (PWR2 vs. power-law) dictates the specific dynamics.
main_assumptions: The semiclassical analysis is performed in the large spin limit ($S 	o \infty$), and the analysis focuses on 1D chains.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of entanglement entropy and QFI density as a function of the number of flips ($k$), showing clear changes in scaling and saturation indicative of the crossover. Other figures plot the semi-classical OTOC to extract the Lyapunov exponent.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model and the two regimes, then systematically varies the initial state symmetry (by changing $k$) while monitoring quantum measures (EE, QFI) and semiclassical chaos indicators ($\lambda_L$) to map out the crossover.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between initial state symmetry and the resulting quantum dynamics (collective vs. scrambling) provides a powerful, tunable control mechanism highly relevant for experimental quantum simulation platforms like neutral atoms in cavities.
